subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram first-run setup move to token-verified owner capture that writes dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom, or should pairing remain the default with stronger warnings/manual setup?
rationale: This changes who can request access to a bundled private bot during first-run setup, and maintainers need to choose the trust boundary, compatibility behavior, and UX tradeoff before implementation.

options.title: Adopt verified owner capture
options.body: Fresh Telegram setup displays a short token, captures only the matching sender ID, and stores allowlist mode for that owner by default.

options.title: Keep pairing default with warnings
options.body: Current pairing behavior remains the default while setup and docs more strongly route one-owner deployments to manual numeric allowlists.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap design
options.body: This narrow request remains open as context while the larger localhost plus Telegram bootstrap surface in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48471 defines the product contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt verified owner capture
recommendation.body: Fresh Telegram setup displays a short token, captures only the matching sender ID, and stores allowlist mode for that owner by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Telegram setup, docs, config defaults, and security-default policy where current review history and code history point most strongly to steipete.
